evals.prompt: Define performance testing in 2-3 sentences. Include controlled load, non-functional properties, SLO thresholds, and how it differs from functional correctness testing.
expected_elements: Measures non-functional properties such as latency, throughput, error rate, resource use, or saturation
Runs the system under controlled load
Verifies against explicit SLO or threshold targets
Distinguishes from functional tests that check correct output
Mentions offline/controlled measurement rather than production observability

evals.prompt: Explain the mental model of performance testing. Name at least 8 primitives and explain how they connect.
expected_elements: At least 8 of: load profile, workload mix, latency percentile, throughput, error rate, resource utilization, saturation, SLO, threshold, environment fidelity, load generator, coordinated omission, duration
Explains workload plus load shape produces measured metrics
Explains SLO thresholds turn measurements into pass/fail verdicts
Explains environment fidelity determines what the result actually certifies
Explains percentiles expose tail behavior that averages hide

evals.prompt: Why does this skill exist? Name the failure modes it prevents.
expected_elements: Prevents intuition-based claims that a system is fast enough
Prevents measurements without SLO verdicts
Prevents average-latency acceptance criteria
Prevents testing an unrealistic workload or environment
Prevents missing leak/degradation failures that require soak tests
Prevents confusing optimization work with measurement work

evals.prompt: Distinguish performance testing from performance engineering, performance budgets, observability, testing strategy, integration/e2e tests, and mutation testing.
expected_elements: performance-engineering profiles and optimizes slow paths
performance-budgets declares thresholds and consequences
observability measures production runtime behavior
testing-strategy chooses the overall mix and cadence of test levels
integration/e2e tests own correctness across seams or user journeys
mutation-testing measures whether the test suite catches defects
performance-testing owns controlled-load measurement and verification

evals.prompt: Classify smoke, load, stress, spike, soak, and breakpoint tests. What does each verify?
expected_elements: Smoke verifies the script/system functions under tiny load
Load/average verifies SLO at expected traffic
Stress verifies behavior beyond expected capacity and graceful failure
Spike verifies sudden load increase, elasticity, and recovery
Soak verifies leaks and degradation over time
Breakpoint gradually increases to failure to quantify capacity ceiling

evals.prompt: Give an analogy for performance testing that preserves controlled load, instrumentation, SLO verdicts, and failure-mode discovery. Then name one bad analogy.
expected_elements: Uses bridge/load-bearing, stress rig, or capacity inspection analogy
Maps known load to traffic profile
Maps instrumentation to latency/resource/error metrics
Maps SLOs to pass/fail acceptance
Rejects a bad analogy that treats a single happy-path request or average as enough

evals.prompt: Novel scenario: A team reports average latency of 80ms from a staging load test, but p99 is 4s, the workload is all reads, and production has mixed reads/writes and larger data. Diagnose the test quality and repair it.
expected_elements: Rejects average latency as acceptance criterion
Uses p95/p99 thresholds tied to SLOs
Flags unrealistic workload mix
Flags environment/data fidelity gap
Requires error rate, throughput, resource, and saturation metrics
Does not certify production readiness from the reported test

evals.prompt: Correct this statement: 'The load test passed because average latency was good and the server handled the requested RPS for five minutes.'
expected_elements: Corrects average latency to percentile/distribution acceptance
Requires explicit SLO thresholds
Mentions duration and load shape must match the failure mode
Mentions error rate and resource/saturation metrics
Warns five minutes cannot reveal soak/leak issues
Mentions generator/coordinated omission concerns when relevant
